info.bio:
Brian Wilson era componente y compositor de las canciones de los Beach boys y que en 1966 rivalizaba  con los beatles para tratar de crear el "sonido perfecto". Llego un punto que lo consiguió tras no obedecer a su compañía discográfica y componer a finales de ese año un disco realmente armonico, personal y de autor como fue "Pet Sounds". Este disco fue un éxito rotundo en cuanto a critica, pero un fracaso en cuanto a ventas.
Mas tarde Paul

scenes.name: The Beach Boys y Brian Wilson
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Eclipsado por los Beatles desde 1964, Brian Wilson se quedó grabando en Los Ángeles mientras el grupo giraba y, inspirado por Rubber Soul, hizo de Pet Sounds (mayo de 1966) un álbum de ambiente sobre la pérdida, la alienación y el fin de la adolescencia, con letras de Tony Asher: ternura y vulnerabilidad frente al frío mod de los Stones. En Estados Unidos vendió menos de lo esperado; en Gran Bretaña, con Derek Taylor de propagandista («un genio»), arrasó. «Good Vibrations» (octubre), grabada por secciones de febrero a septiembre y editada como un mosaico, con cellos y electro-theremin, costó 50.000 dólares: una canción psicodélica sobre la comunicación no verbal que nació de un recuerdo de infancia y del LSD. Fue número 1 en Gran Bretaña el 19 de noviembre tras su visita a Londres: el centro del pop se había movido de Londres a Los Ángeles. Pero algo siniestro latía detrás: grabando SMiLE, el 28 de noviembre Wilson hizo tocar con cascos de bombero «Mrs. O’Leary’s Fire», una de las piezas más aterradoras de Los Ángeles, y la repudió días después.

podcast.title: Childhood Trauma and Mental Health
podcast.body: Wilson faced profound personal challenges stemming from pressure and mistreatment by his father during childhood, which left deep roots affecting his mental well-being. These issues, combined with immense pressure to surpass the successes of Pet Sounds and "Good Vibrations," were exacerbated by his abuse of hallucinogenic substances, likely contributing to his mental problems. "La presión y los maltratos que sufrió de niño por parte de su padre le dejaron raíces profundas que afectaron a su bienestar mental."

podcast.title: Creative Obsession and Perfectionism
podcast.body: Wilson was consumed by the desire to be the best in composition, arrangement, and recording, aiming to surpass Paul McCartney in composition, Phil Spector in production, and compete with the finest arrangers of his era. His meticulous process, evident in "Good Vibrations," was a preview of his aspirations for Smile. "Wilson se encargaba de la composición, arreglo, sigrabación y querías ser el mejor en todos ellos."

podcast.title: Emotional State during Pet Sounds
podcast.body: Brian Wilson's emotionally damaged state at the time of the album's creation is cited as a factor by some emo researchers when considering The Beach Boys' "Pet Sounds" as an early progenitor of emo music. "the fact that he was so emotionally damaged at the time."

podcast.title: Genius and Maestro Status
podcast.body: Following the release of Pet Sounds, Brian Wilson was elevated to the stature of a musical genius and maestro, acknowledged for his pivotal role in creating new and exciting paths for music. "ha elevado a Bryan Wilson, la cabeza detrás del álbum, a la altura de Gienio de la música."

podcast.title: Impact of "Strawberry Fields Forever"
podcast.body: The release of The Beatles' single "Strawberry Fields Forever" in February 1967 is often cited as a breaking point for Brian Wilson and the Smile project. He reportedly felt that The Beatles had achieved what he had so desperately yearned for. "Otro punto que se comenta que fue el desencadenante del fíntil disco es el lanzamiento del single Strawberry Hills Forever de los Beatles, en febrero de 1967, al sentir que ellos habían logrado lo que él tanto ansiaba."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Panic Attacks and Stage Fright
podcast.body: In late 1964, Brian Wilson suffered an extremely intense and distressing panic attack during a flight. This incident led him to stop touring and playing live with The Beach Boys due to stage fright, allowing him to concentrate entirely on compositional tasks. "Wilson sufrió un ataque de panico durante un vuelo, un evento que fue para él extremadamente intenso y angustioso."

srcs.episode: El Álbum Perdido que pudo cambiar la música ｜ Smile de The Beach Boys

podcast.title: Paranoia during Smile Production
podcast.body: As the Smile project unraveled, Brian Wilson became increasingly paranoid. He feared that The Beatles might steal his songs and even believed he was the target of a conspiracy led by Phil Spector. "Bryan estaba cada vez más paranoico, temía que los Beatles pudieran robarle las canciones, incluso llegó a pensar que era el blanco de una conspiración encabezada por Fille Spector."

podcast.title: Potential Outsider Musician
podcast.body: Brian Wilson of The Beach Boys is suggested as a potential inclusion in discussions of outsider music, particularly when considering his entire life story. "I could have also included Brian Wilson of the Beach Boys, which makes total sense, but only if you know his entire life story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Profound Reaction to "Be My Baby"
podcast.body: Brian Wilson of The Beach Boys was so deeply affected upon first hearing "Be My Baby" on his car radio that he reportedly had to pull over to the side of the road. He later listened to the record incessantly for hours, indicating a significant personal and musical impact. "Brian Wilson of The Beach Boys talks to this day about how he had to pull over to the side of the road when he first heard it on his car radio, and he would listen to the record incessantly for hours at a time."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 110: "Be My Baby" by the Ronettes

podcast.title: Retreat and Reclusion
podcast.body: Following the cancellation of Smile and the subsequent perceived decline of The Beach Boys, Brian Wilson significantly reduced his compositional role and increasingly withdrew into the reclusion of his home, marking a period of deep personal and professional retreat. "Brian Wilson redujo significativamente su rol compositivo y se retiró cada vez más a la reclusión de su hogar."

podcast.title: Unrealized Production of "Seasons in the Sun"
podcast.body: Brian Wilson of The Beach Boys had specific creative ideas for "Seasons in the Sun," which almost became a Beach Boys single, but the song's original artist, Terry Jackson, did not have the patience to see Wilson's vision through. "that was very close to becoming a Beach Boys single, but Jackson did not have the patience for all the things that Brian Wilson wanted to do with that song."

xref.title: Brian Wilson Death (2025) – Respiratory Failure and Sepsis After Long COVID
xref.body: Brian Wilson, creative genius of The Beach Boys, died in 2025. He had battled mental health issues since the 1960s and subsequent cognitive decline. His death was complicated by long COVID contracted in 2022, which led to respiratory failure and sepsis. "His death was complicated by long COVID contracted in 2022, leading to respiratory failure and sepsis."
